text:
maria: Heads-up — after pushing the 560.12 driver to us-west2-gpu pool, ~12 nodes failed to come back with DKMS rebuild errors. Rolling deploy started ~1789645600.

infra-bot: alert: node-reboot: gpu-node-47 failed health checks, cordoned and marked for investigation :rotating_light:

kyle: seen that. Errors when modprobe tries to load nvidia_uvm and nvidia_drm. DKMS logs show build for kernel 6.1.19-rc1 failing with: 
```
ERROR (dkms apport): kernel/source/..:__ia32__/module.c: unresolved symbol: nv_pci_probe
make[2]: *** [module] Error 1
```

juan: any secureboot on those hosts? We had a similar stack when modules weren't signed.

olivia: us-west2-gpu nodes are mixed — some have Secure Boot on, some off. The ones failing are mostly SB=enabled.

kyle: that matches. 560 seems to ship unsigned modules by default when DKMS path used. For signed kernels with SB enabled, modprobe rejects them.

maria: can we patch DKMS job to sign modules with our internal key? That might be faster than full rollback.

sre-rotation: signing is possible but we need the private key access + machine signing agent installed; will take ~2h to enable safely. Also need to update initramfs on those nodes.

juan: short-term: can we put a host-level workaround to disable module signature verification? riskier but fastest.

olivia: not comfortable flipping SB off in prod without CTL approval. We should avoid bit-flipping.

maria: deploy-bot — can we trigger a controlled rollback to 535.x on the remaining nodes in the canary pool? Keep the 12 failed nodes cordoned until we have a plan.

deploy-bot: Started rollback job: rollback/nvidia-driver-560 -> nvidia-driver-535 on pool=us-west2-gpu-canary (12 nodes target). See CI job https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/rollbacks/8721 :gear:

infra-bot: telemetry: failed DKMS builds spike at 2026-03-15T09:02:18Z, correlates with rolling window.

kyle: notes from quick triage: NV package changed build flags (LC_ALL unset) which surfaces a compiler warning -> treated as error in our DKMS wrapper. Patch available upstream but not yet released.

maria: patching DKMS wrapper on hundreds of nodes is heavy. I'd prefer rollback + hotfix release. Rollback in progress for canary; schedule gate for remaining pools until hotfix validated.

juan: also seeing nvidia-persistenced OOM on a few nodes during rebuilds causing node eviction. Need to increase oom_score_adj or restart policy.

olivia: changed systemd override on one node to restart always, node came back but kernel messages show: 
```
kernel: nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel
kernel: nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol nv_map_user_pages
```

maria: good capture. We should add a short-run runbook in #incidents for engineers who hit this. Steps: 1) cordon node 2) check /var/lib/dkms/<pkg>/build/make.log 3) inspect secureboot (`mokutil --sb-state`) 4) if SB enabled escalate to SRE 5) rollback via deploy job if needed.

sre-rotation: adding runbook snippet now. 

infra-bot: runbook update: https://confluence.redwood-inference.internal/runbooks/dkms-driver-failure (draft) :memo:

kyle: FYI for next release: ask NV to provide signed module artifacts for our DKMS path or change package to use prebuilt modules for supported kernels. Also add CI gating that builds drivers against our Secure Boot kernels.

juan: cost note — keep in mind rollback will extend the rolling window and double some GPU-hours; estimated extra cost ~ $1.6k for the next 24h if we slow the rollout.

maria: acknowledged. Prioritize correctness over cost here — several training jobs hit node evictions.

olivia: quick status: canary rollback completed on 8/12 nodes; 4 still in progress (one stuck in reboot loop).

infra-bot: node gpu-node-51 reboot-loop detected, attaching serial logs to ticket #INC-8273.

maria: for the stuck node, please capture full dmesg and early printk. If kernel complaining about 'nvidia: module verification failed', we shouldn't attempt reboots without plan.

juan: I'll attach a debug image and escalate to hardware owners if it looks like firmware mismatch.

maria: thanks team. Next actions: (1) finish canary rollback (kyle + deploy-bot) (2) SRE to prepare signing flow or kernel module packaging plan (sre-rotation) (3) Draft customer comms for impacted clusters if rollback extends past 4h (maria).

kyle: working on rollback automation now, ping me for access if you want to watch the job. :eyes:

olivia: thanks all. I'll monitor the pool metrics and post updates to #customer-impact if ETA slips. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria: closing loop for now — reopen if we see new nodes failing after 560 patch. :white_check_mark:
